content: This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current medical condition. It should not be used for any other purpose unless directed by your healthcare provider. Missed Dose Instructions: If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Storage Guidelines: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary of the medication and does not include all possible information. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details about this medication and your individual health needs. Uses: This medication is used to treat a specific parasitic infection of the intestines known as amebiasis. It belongs to a class of drugs called aminoglycoside antibiotics. It works by inhibiting the growth of parasites in the intestines. Additionally, paromomycin may be used in combination with a special diet to manage hepatic encephalopathy, a serious brain condition caused by excessive ammonia levels in the body, typically seen in individuals with liver disease. Normally, the liver removes ammonia from the body. This antibiotic is effective only against parasitic and bacterial infections. It is not effective for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, abdominal cramps, diarrhea, and heartburn. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before taking paromomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin, tobramycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Paromomycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor.
